{"description":"Step 6 of `flow:release-cut`.

ONLY ONE COMMIT IN THE INCREMENT MAY TOUCH `docs/design/reflow2.json`. A squash keeps only the last `prev_content_hash`, so two exporting commits leave the chain pointing at an intermediate `main` never saw (BL-156). Fold with `git reset --soft`, then restore the file FROM `origin/main` — never from the branch, because `export_graph` builds `prev_content_hash` from whatever file is already at that path, and exporting over the branch's own copy chains to a document about to be amended out of existence.

EXPORT DIRECTLY FROM THE REAL STORE WITH THE NEW BINARY. The temp-store replay route injects schema defaults the source never stated — 182 injected values on the v0.28.0 cut, and `export_via_binary.py` now prints its own refusal saying so. `--export` is stdout-only and a copied stdout export has no lineage at all.

⚠️ REBUILD AFTER THE VERSION BUMP, NOT BEFORE — ADDED 2026-08-30 AFTER GETTING IT WRONG ON THE v0.45.0 CUT. "The freshly built binary" is not the same as "a binary built recently". The daemon was refreshed, came back reporting the PREVIOUS version, and would have stamped the export with it; the bump had happened after the build. Caught by reading `--version` off the binary rather than trusting that a rebuild had occurred. Order that works: bump every version claim → accept the drift → `cargo build` → refresh → export → verify the stamp.

VERIFY THREE THINGS IN THE WRITTEN FILE before committing: `stamp.reflow2_version` is the new version, `prev_content_hash` equals main's `content_hash`, and injected-value counts are unchanged against the baseline.

═══ THE RECORDED COST IS NARROWER THAN IT SAID — MEASURED 2026-08-30 ═══

This entry read *"it is last of the graph work because it is destructive of MCP access"* and *"killing the server ends MCP tool access for the session"*. THAT IS TRUE OF `kill -TERM` ON THE LOCK HOLDER AND FALSE OF `--stop-shared`. On the v0.45.0 cut the daemon was refreshed TWICE with `reflow2-mcp --graph-path <path> --stop-shared`, and MCP tool access survived both times — the client respawned from the binary on disk, which is the behaviour the stale-server note has claimed since 2026-08-11 and which nothing had exercised during a cut.

⇒ SO THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT IS WEAKER THAN RECORDED. Graph writes do not have to be finished before the refresh; they only have to be finished before the EXPORT, which is a different and much smaller claim. Keeping the old wording would go on making cuts more rigid than they need to be.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the `fuser`/`kill -TERM` route is still needed at all, or whether `--stop-shared` covers every case a cut meets. Only the `--stop-shared` path was exercised, twice, on one machine.



FROM THE MOVE ON (phase 2 of dec:idea-reflow2s-own-design-moves-onto-flo2-io-or-stays-local): the cut writes its record on flo2.io, which still runs the previous release. This step becomes the copy, taken by the cut's freshly built binary: `REFLOW2_BIN=target/release/reflow2-mcp python3 tools/reflow2_design_copy.py copy` (cap:a-design-pr-holds-reflow2s-hosted-design-and-copies-it-in-last). No server is stopped, no session loses MCP, and the cut holds the design like any design PR. Measured 2026-10-10: an export from 0.81.0, imported and exported by 0.81.1, kept its content hash exactly.
